
# Get bigWigs of interest

```{r}
groups <- unique(anno[, c("Subcortex_Group_v4", "Subcortex_Class_v4")]) %>% 
    `rownames<-`(NULL) %>% 
    setNames(c("group", "class"))

groups_use  <- sort(grep("Astro", groups$group, value=T))
# [1] "Astro-NT NN" "Astro-TE NN" "Astro-WM NN"

classes_use <- unique(groups$class) %>% setdiff(c("Nonneuron", "Pineal Gland"))
#  [1] "THM GABA"       "BG"             "CNU-HTH GABA"   "THM Glut"       "HTH Glut"      
#  [6] "CNU-HTH Glut"   "MB-HB Glut"     "MB-HB GABA"     "CTX-CGE GABA"   "CTX-MGE GABA"  
# [11] "HTH GABA"       "HTH Hist"       "TEL Glut"       "SEP GABA"       "MB-HTH-HB Sero"

regroups <- list("Other Nonneuerons" = {
    filter(groups, class=="Nonneuron", !group %in% groups_use)$group
})
# $`Other Nonneuerons`
#  [1] "Oligo OPALIN"  "Oligo PLEKHG1" "COP"           "ImOligo"       "OPC"          
#  [6] "Ependymal"     "BAM"           "VLMC"          "Endo"          "ABC"          
# [11] "Pericyte"      "SMC"           "Tanycyte"      "Microglia"  
```

I chose coordinates after looking in IGV.

```{r}
import_range <- GRanges(seqnames = "chr4", ranges = IRanges(134900000, 135170000))
```

```{r}
bw <- sapply(groups_use, function(x) {
    pth <- file.path(pdir_bw, "Subcortex_Group_v4/cpm", paste0(x, ".bw"))
    import(pth, which = import_range)
}, simplify = FALSE)

bw <- c(bw, sapply(classes_use, function(x) {
    pth <- file.path(pdir_bw, "Subcortex_Class_v4/cpm", paste0(x, ".bw"))
    import(pth, which = import_range)
}))
```

For the "regroups" (basically recombining all the Nonneurons together), will
have to be done a little differently because the CPM normalization will be 
broken. I will just average the CPM scores for each group within the region.

```{r}
bw_regroup <- sapply(regroups$`Other Nonneuerons`, function(x) {
    pth <- file.path(pdir_bw, "Subcortex_Group_v4/cpm", paste0(x, ".bw"))
    import(pth, which = import_range)
}, simplify = FALSE)

# divide CPM signal by number of groups before merging
bw_regroup <- lapply(bw_regroup, function(x) {
    score(x) <- score(x) / length(bw_regroup)
    x
})

bw$`Other Nonneurons` <- BRGenomics::mergeGRangesData(bw_regroup)
```

We'll see how that works out.

```{r}
bw <- lapply(bw, makeGRangesBRG)
```

# Get useable annotations

```{r}

```

also enhancers

genes

```{r}
enhs <- GRanges(c(
    "E1" = "chr4:135137891-135138392",
    "E2" = "chr4:135137386-135137887",
    "E3" = "chr4:135119184-135119685",
    "E4" = "chr4:134932591-134933092"
))
strand(enhs) <- "*"
```

```{r}
gns_ens <- c(gns, enhs)
```

# Summary

In the end it's browser shot4 being used, with the genemodel being resized
and substituted in for the genearrow, but the genearrow plot being the one 
used because it marks the exact enhancer locations.

# Version 2 (with zooms)

The entire region being plotted results in the individual peaks being really
small. So I will try to make a new version that zooms in on several loci.

One thing I need to figure out is how to show the entire region up to. One
idea is showing loops, which I can make simply in Illustrator.

But for that, I need a plot that shows the gene, each of the enhancers, and the
zoom regions being used.


```{r}
subsetByOverlaps(gns_ens, import_range)
```

## Plot whole region with zooms

```{r}
# zoom1 = 10kb upstream MOXD1 TSS to 10kb downstream of E3 [=38.982kb]
# zoom2 = 10kb upstream to 10kb downstream of E4
zooms <- GRanges("chr4", IRanges(
    c(135109184, 134922591),
    c(135148166, 134943092)
))
names(zooms) <- c("zoom1", "zoom2")

p_region_zoom1 <- shot_genearrow(
    import_range,
    c(gns_ens, zooms),
    gene_names = c(names(gns_ens), names(zooms))
)
```

```{r}
ggsave(
    file.path("zoom_wholeRegion1.pdf"),
    p_region_zoom1 & theme(
        axis.text.y = txt,
        strip.text = txt
    ),
    # width=90, height=60, units="mm"
    width=170, height=30, units="mm"
)
```

also need the gene model

```{r}
p_region_mod <- shot_genemodel(
    import_range,
    txdb
)
```

